summary: Seymour Galapagos Ecological Airport (GPS) is the principal gateway to the Galápagos Islands, located on the small, arid Isla Baltra. Originally constructed as a U.S. military base during World War II to protect the Panama Canal, the airport was later redesigned as one of the world's most eco-friendly terminals, built largely from recycled materials. It serves as the main arrival point for travelers heading to Santa Cruz and beyond in the archipelago.

Q: How do I get from Seymour Airport to Puerto Ayora?
A: After landing, take the free shuttle bus to the Itabaca Channel, cross by ferry to Santa Cruz Island, then continue by bus or taxi to Puerto Ayora. The total journey typically takes around 1.5 to 2 hours.
